arxiv-2010-11856.title: Xor QA: Cross-lingual Open-Retrieval Question Answering
arxiv-2010-11856.creator: Akari Asai, Jungo Kasai, Jonathan H. Clark, Kenton Lee, Eunsol Choi, Hannaneh Hajishirzi
arxiv-2010-11856.description: Abstract Multilingual question answering tasks typically assume that answers exist in the same language as the question. Yet in practice, many languages face both information scarcity —where languages have few reference articles—and information asymmetry —where questions reference concepts from other cultures.

arxiv-2402-09500.title: On Formally Undecidable Traits of Intelligent Machines
arxiv-2402-09500.creator: Matthew Fox matthew.fox@colorado.edu
arxiv-2402-09500.description: Abstract Building on work by ? (?), we study the conditions necessary for it to be logically possible to prove that an arbitrary artificially intelligent machine will exhibit certain behavior. To do this, we develop a formalism like—but mathematically distinct from—the theory of formal languages and their properties.

arxiv-2411-15101.title: What You See is Not What You Get: Neural Partial Differential Equations and The Illusion of Learning
arxiv-2411-15101.creator: Arvind Mohan, Ashesh Chattopadhyay, Jonah Miller
arxiv-2411-15101.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Arvind Mohan, Ashesh Chattopadhyay, Jonah Miller. Differentiable Programming for scientific machine learning (SciML) has recently seen considerable interest and success, as it directly embeds neural networks inside PDEs, often called as NeuralPDEs, derived from first principle physics. Unlike large, parameterized black-box deep neural networks, NeuralPDEs promise a targeted and efficient learning approach by only representing unknown terms and allowing the rest of the known PDE to constrain the network with known physics.

arxiv-2506-03301.title: From Instructions to 𝑂𝐷𝑅𝐿 \mathit{ODRL} Usage Policies: An Ontology Guided Approach
arxiv-2506-03301.creator: Daham M. Mustafa, Abhishek Nadgeri, Diego Collarana, Benedikt T. Arnold, Christoph Quix, Christoph Lange, Stefan Decker
arxiv-2506-03301.description: Abstract This study presents an approach that uses large language models such as GPT-4 to generate usage policies in the W3C Open Digital Rights Language 𝑂𝐷𝑅𝐿 \mathit{ODRL} automatically from natural language instructions. Our approach uses the 𝑂𝐷𝑅𝐿 \mathit{ODRL} ontology and its documentation as a central part of the prompt.

arxiv-2511-02210.title: Estimation of Segmental Longitudinal Strain in Transesophageal Echocardiography by Deep Learning
arxiv-2511-02210.creator: Anders Austlid Taskén, Thierry Judge, Erik Andreas Rye Berg, Jinyang Yu, Bjørnar Grenne, Frank Lindseth, Svend Aakhus, Pierre-Marc Jodoin, Nicolas Duchateau, Olivier Bernard, Gabriel Kiss
arxiv-2511-02210.description: Abstract Segmental longitudinal strain (SLS) of the left ventricle (LV) is an important prognostic indicator for evaluating regional LV dysfunction, in particular for diagnosing and managing myocardial ischemia. Current techniques for strain estimation require significant manual intervention and expertise, limiting their efficiency and making them too resource-intensive for monitoring purposes.

arxiv-2511-03086.title: Speech-Based Prioritization for Schizophrenia Intervention
arxiv-2511-03086.creator: Gowtham Premananth, Philip Resnik, Sonia Bansal, Deanna L.Kelly, Carol Espy-Wilson
arxiv-2511-03086.description: Abstract Millions of people suffer from mental health conditions, yet many remain undiagnosed or receive delayed care due to limited clinical resources and labor-intensive assessment methods. While most machine-assisted approaches focus on diagnostic classification, estimating symptom severity is essential for prioritizing care, particularly in resource-constrained settings.

arxiv-2601-15500.title: Low-Dimensional Adaptation of Rectified Flow: A Diffusion and Stochastic Localization Perspective
arxiv-2601-15500.creator: Saptarshi Roy, Alessandro Rinaldo, Purnamrita Sarkar
arxiv-2601-15500.description: Abstract In recent years, Rectified flow (RF) has gained considerable popularity largely due to its generation efficiency and state-of-the-art performance. In this paper, we investigate how well RF automatically adapts to the intrinsic low dimensionality of the support of the target distribution to accelerate sampling.

arxiv-2602-09436.title: Principal spectral theory and asymptotic analysis for time-periodic cooperative systems with temporally nonlocal dispersal Thanks: 1 School of Mathematics and Statistics, Lanzhou University, Lanzhou, Gansu 730000, China. 2 Faculty of Mathematics and Applications, Saigon University, Ho Chi Minh City,
arxiv-2602-09436.creator: Hao Wu 1 , Wan-Tong Li 1,∗ , Jian-Wen Sun 1 and Hoang-Hung Vo 2
arxiv-2602-09436.description: Abstract . This paper investigates the principal spectral theory and the asymptotic behavior of the principal spectrum point for a class of time-periodic cooperative systems with nonlocal dispersal operators, incorporating both coupled and uncoupled nonlocal terms. By applying the theory of resolvent positive operators and their perturbations, we first establish criteria for the existence of the principal eigenvalue.

pmc-11693032.title: PARTICIPATION IN VALUED ACTIVITIES, RESTRICTION, AND SOCIAL ISOLATION IN DEMENTIA CAREGIVING
pmc-11693032.creator: Sarah Won, Valerie Cotter, Chakra Budhathoki, Natalie Regier
pmc-11693032.description: This study investigated the associations between five indicators of social determinants of health (SDOH) and participation in valued activities, participation restriction, and social isolation among family and other unpaid caregivers of older adults with dementia. Data from the 2022 National Health and Aging Trends Study and National Study of Caregiving IV (Round 12) were analyzed.

pmc-11728781.creator: Márcia Carvalho, Manuela Matos, António Crespí, Violeta R. Lopes, Valdemar Carnide

pmc-12534532.title: Exploratory approach to speculate on body composition models for elite teenage basketball players
pmc-12534532.creator: Mario Mauro, Federica Moro, Stefania Toselli
pmc-12534532.description: The study of human body composition covers many fields, from clinical assessment to sports performance. Humans manifest different traits that set limitations in model estimation. This investigation aimed to (i) provide sport-specific densities for reducing biological variation in body composition assessment, and (ii) develop new regression models for body volume and density estimation by field applications.

pmc-12608376.title: Efficacy of Autologous Conditioned Serum on the Dorsal Root Ganglion in Patients with Chronic Radicular Pain: Prospective Randomized Placebo-Controlled Double Blind Clinical Trial (RADISAC Trial)
pmc-12608376.creator: Marta Homs, Raimon Milà, Jordi Recasens, Diego Delgado, Rosa Maria Borràs, Ricard Valdés, David Parés, Gian Marco Petroni
pmc-12608376.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background: Pulsed radiofrequency (PRF) applied to the dorsal root ganglion (DRG) has been proposed as an effective neuromodulator treatment for persistent radicular pain. Autologous conditioned serum (ACS) therapy, derived from the patient’s own blood, offers a conservative approach. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy of ACS applied to the DRG as an adjunct in treating lower limb radicular pain (LLRP).

pmc-13053443.title: Integrative multimodal transcriptomics identifies a cancer-associated fibroblast membrane signature for predicting prognosis and therapeutic response in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
pmc-13053443.creator: Leshi Zhuang, Wei Zhang, Jun Wu, Jian Cao, Liang Feng, Shubo Cao
pmc-13053443.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are central to the pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) microenvironment, promoting tumor progression and therapeutic resistance. However, the expression landscape of CAF membrane proteins in PDAC remains poorly defined. We integrated scRNA-seq (n = 33; 87,949 cells), spatial transcriptomics (n = 2; 7,011 spots), and bulk RNA-seq (n = 7; 642 samples) to systematically identify PDAC-specific CAF membrane genes. A LASSO-based Cox model was developed to construct a prognostic signature, PaFMS, and evaluated through multi-cohort validation.

pmc-13410701.creator: Steven J Edwards, Benjamin J Burgess, Nicole Downes, Sophie Ip, Archie Walters, Clare Dadswell
pmc-13410701.description: ObjectivesTo review how statistically non-significant indirect treatment comparison (ITC) results are interpreted within National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) cost-comparison evaluations (CCEs) and develop a framework to support interpretations of these results from Bayesian network meta-analyses (NMAs).DesignA systematic review of CCEs between 2017 (first introduced) and April 2025.

pmc-13418907.title: Brain Shift Patterns: Upward, Lateral and Downward Herniation, Its Correlation with Clinical Patterns in Acute Intracranial Pathologies and Neurosurgical Management
pmc-13418907.creator: Nur Nazleen Said Mogutham, Jafri Malin Abdullah, Suzuanhafizan Omar, Mohammad Iskandar Sa’uadi, Sharifah Nawal Syed Jaafar
pmc-13418907.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Brain shift is a critical radiological indicator of intracranial mass effect, resulting from haematoma, tumour, infarction, or cerebral oedema. Depending on the direction of displacement, herniation may occur as downward transtentorial, upward (reverse transtentorial), or lateral midline shift (MLS). This study aims to classify brain shift patterns and correlate radiological findings with clinical parameters, including level of consciousness, Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS), pupillary size and reactivity, and predicted intracranial pressure (ICP).

pmc-13603211.title: Canvas of Strength: A Mixed-Methods Pilot Study of a Community-Based Arts Intervention for Women Survivors of Domestic Violence in China
pmc-13603211.creator: Xingcen Liu, Kamal Sabran
pmc-13603211.description: Women survivors of domestic violence often experience persistent psychological distress, yet evidence supporting community-based arts interventions remains limited, particularly in mainland China. This mixed-methods pilot study evaluated the preliminary effectiveness of Canvas of Strength, a community-based arts intervention for women survivors of domestic violence in Liaoning Province, China.

uslaw-usc-t15-s7602.title: 15 U.S.C. § 7602 — Immediate payment of fees in limited circumstances
uslaw-usc-t15-s7602.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t15-s7602.description: United States Code, Title 15 (Commerce And Trade); Chapter 102 (Fairness To Contact Lens Consumers). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. A prescriber may require payment of fees for an eye examination, fitting, and evaluation before the release of a contact lens prescription, but only if the prescriber requires immediate payment in the case of an examination that reveals no requirement for ophthalmic.
